subject: Anchoring usage tiers & support matrix for on‑prem deployment
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the model performance looked promising for our transcription workflows. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how Redwood structures fees for on‑prem (VPC) installs when we exceed the initial committed throughput. Two specific asks:

1) How do you anchor usage tiers (commit bands) for on‑prem customers — is it flat nodes, vCPU equivalents, or token throughput?
2) We need a clear mapping of support tiers (response SLA, oncall hours, number of incident rollups) tied to those tiers and any add‑ons for 24/7 coverage.

Can you share a simple matrix we can review with legal + infra?

— Ari
Procurement, Meadow Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Hi Ari — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attached is a compact matrix (meadow_vpc_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx) that maps three anchoring approaches we typically offer: committed GPU/node counts, sustained token throughput bands, and a hybrid seat+node model for mixed‑workloads.

Quick notes:
- Anchor recommendation: for infra teams that want predictability we suggest node commits (GPU equivalent) paired with a short overage rate by token during spikes.
- If you expect volatile peaks but low baseline, the hybrid band gives a lower platform fee but higher burst cost.
- Platform fee is separate from support; support tiers (attached support_tier_descriptions.pdf) are stackable.

I copied Sean (sales engineering) and Neha (commercial ops) so they can confirm SLA details and provide a conservative numeric example for Meadow. Would you prefer the matrix in USD or as a percentage uplift to a base seat price?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Ari — copied below are three short examples to make the tradeoffs clearer (numbers are indicative):

Example A — Predictable commit (node anchor):
- Commit: 8x A100-equivalent nodes (preferred for steady throughput)
- Platform fee: $18k/mo (flat)
- Support: Standard (business hours, 8x5) included; Premium (24/7) +$6k/mo
- Overage: token bursts charged at $0.0005/token beyond sustained limits

Example B — Hybrid (seat + burst):
- Commit: 4 developer seats + 4 nodes baseline
- Platform fee: $11k/mo
- Burst pool: metered at $0.0009/token but burst credit pools can be purchased monthly
- Support: Premium included with enterprise seat packs; white-glove support priced separately

Example C — Throughput‑anchored:
- Commit: 250k tokens/min sustained
- Platform fee: $22k/mo (higher to cover autoscaling/capacity reservation)
- Overage: lower marginal token price $0.00035/token for sustained bursts

Attached excel has line items and an aide to map Meadow’s projected monthly token shape so we can recommend an anchor. If you share a 30‑day sample we’ll run the model and highlight the lowest total cost mix.

— Sean
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Thanks Sean/Kimberly — helpful context. A couple of clarifying questions from infra:

1) If we anchor on nodes, how do you handle version upgrades that require rolling restarts? Is that included in platform fee or billed as a migration/ops effort?
2) For the Premium support SLA, what is the escalation path (pager oncall -> engineering -> SE) and the guaranteed MTTR at each severity level?

Also attaching a 30‑day sample token histogram (not an attachment in this thread for privacy) — would prefer a consolidated recommendation that minimizes our month‑to‑month variability.

Sofia
Director of Engineering, Meadow Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Sofia — quick answers while we finalize the matrix: 

1) Upgrades & rolling restarts: minor patch and minor version upgrades are included in the platform fee with a standard maintenance window. Major upgrades or custom backports are scoped as professional services with an estimate. We can include an optional upgrade retainer (+$4k/mo) to cover two major upgrades/year and priority scheduling.

2) Premium SLA escalation path & MTTR (example):
- Sev 1 (production down): Pager immediately routes to SE oncall, target ack 15 minutes, target MTTR 4 hours (with on‑site option negotiable).
- Sev 2 (severe degradation): Ack 30 minutes, MTTR 8 hours.
- Sev 3 (minor impact): Ack 4 business hours, MTTR 3 business days.

If Meadow wants a contractual MTTR we will include it in the SOW and attach service credits for breaches. For the matrix we recommend anchoring on nodes + a small token buffer for predictable egress costs — this usually minimizes variance for workloads like yours.

I can push an updated matrix by EOD tomorrow that folds in the upgrade retainer and a 24/7 add‑on pricing line.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@meadowhealth.com>, Ari Patel <ari.patel@meadowhealth.com>, procurement@meadowhealth.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — on‑prem pricing structure and support options

Sofia/Ari — thanks for the quick questions. Attached is the updated matrix that includes: node anchor recommendation with a 10% token buffer, explicit upgrade retainer line, and the Premium SLA with contractual MTTRs and service credit language. Key callouts in the worksheet:

- Recommended anchor: 6x A100-equivalent nodes + 10% token buffer based on your 30‑day sample — this keeps monthly variability under 12% in our model.
- Platform fee (node anchor): $13k/mo, Upgrade retainer: $4k/mo, Premium SLA: $6.5k/mo.
- One‑time onboarding SOW for install and integration: $45k (includes 2 weeks on‑site enablement).

Next step: if Meadow approves the anchor we’ll generate a draft SOW + Term Sheet and route to legal for a limited redline window. If procurement prefers a capped overage rather than per‑token billing we can convert the buffer into prepaid burst credits.

I’m happy to jump on a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk the team through the workbook. Proposed times: 10:00am or 2:00pm PT.

Best,
Kimberly
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: meadow_vpc_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), support_tier_descriptions.pdf (pdf)
